chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Durays ibn A'yan, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who set out in Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj) from Umrah to Hajj, and he did not reach Mecca except on the Day of Nahri (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah). He said: 'He remains in his state of Ihram and cuts off the Talbiyah when he enters Mecca, then he performs Tawaf and Sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah, shaves his head, and returns to his family if he wishes.'
And he said: 'This is for the one who made a condition upon his Lord when he entered into Ihram. If he did not make the condition, then upon him is Hajj next year.'
And whoever attends the rituals while intoxicated, there is no Hajj for him. Narrated.

key_terms.الإحرام: Ihram (the sacred state of consecration for pilgrimage)
key_terms.الاشتراط: Conditioning (making a condition upon leaving for a specific outcome)
key_terms.التلبية: Talbiyah (the recitation of 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk' during Hajj)
key_terms.التمتع: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, exits Ihram, and then enters Ihram again for Hajj)
key_terms.اليوم النَّحر: The Day of Sacrifice (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who arrives in Mecca late during the season of Tamattu' Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural nuances of the Tamattu' Hajj, specifically addressing the scenario where a pilgrim arrives in Mecca on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr). It distinguishes between those who stipulated an exit from Ihram after Umrah, allowing them to complete the rites and depart, and those who did not, who remain in the state of Ihram for Hajj. Additionally, it establishes that intoxication invalidates the Hajj obligation, a principle derived from the Quranic command to 'not approach prayer while intoxicated.'
